newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end with record close, banks mixed.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end with record close, banks mixed.

text.p: Swiss indices posted record closing highs in very high volume, pulled up by Wall Street gains and strong demand for pharmaceuticals.
Major banks underperformed the market, which may have been triggered by fears the Swiss banks may face a ban in New York, a dealer noted.
The city and state of New York said on Wednesday they were considering punitive measures against Swiss banks unless Switzerland sets up a fund to support Holocaust victims.

Swiss banks replied they were already rusging to create such a fund with Swiss government. A senior U.S. officials, Commerce Undersecretary Stuart Eizenstat, said in Zurich a boycott would be counterproductive to Swiss efforts to track lost Jewish accounts and Nazi assets.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) firmed 39.2 points, or 0.94 percent, at 4,208.9 points, a shade off the all-time high at 4,215.4 points.
The broad Swiss Market Index (SPI) ended up 22.75 points, or 0.85 percent, to 2,689.38.
Pharmaceuticals and chemicals continued their recent strong performance.
Clariant added 11 francs to 666. The company said 1996 sales rose nine percent to 2.337 billion francs and that earnings were expected to show a double-digit increase.
Roche continued to power ahead after being in the spotlight during the past few session due to various merger and divestment speculations. Roche certificates added 90 francs to 12,000 francs.
Novartis registered shares were up eight francs to 1,613.
Nestle was sought by a major Swiss bank, traders said. It firmed 38 francs, or 2.53 percent, to 1,538. Technical factors and a new study were also seen behind the rise, one dealer said.
Insurer Zurich shot up 12 francs to 398.50 on buying interest from U.S. investors, a dealer noted.
UBS slid eight francs to 1,175, while CS Holding added 0.50 francs to 144.25 and SBC were up 2.50 francs to 236.50.
Surveillance and Sulzer were among the losers in the blue-chip segement.
